## Script for retest analysis 

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr) 
library(readr)

here::i_am("flag_project_root.R")
here::here()
data_path = here::here()
```


# Get data T1 & T2
```{r}
#Add T1/T2 as variable 

df_T1 <- read.csv(paste0(data_path, "/data/retestT1/alldata.csv"),header = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(Time = "T1")

df_T2 <- read.csv(paste0(data_path, "/data/retestT2/alldata.csv"),header = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(Time = "T2")

df <- bind_rows(df_T1, df_T2)


#Some general transformations
# From JSON-like character vectors to actual lists
df <- df %>% mutate(
  csPosition = map(csPosition, ~ if (is.character(.x)) fromJSON(.x) else .x),
  ratingCoordinate = map(ratingCoordinate, ~ if (is.character(.x)) fromJSON(.x) else .x)
)

#split coordinates for CS+ and ratings into two columns 
df <- df %>%
  mutate(csX = map_dbl(csPosition, 1), 
         csY = map_dbl(csPosition, 2)) 

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    rateX = map_dbl(ratingCoordinate, ~ if (length(.x) == 2) .x[[1]] else 0),
    rateY = map_dbl(ratingCoordinate, ~ if (length(.x) == 2) .x[[2]] else 0)
  )

#adjust for 1 indexing 
df$csX = df$csX+1
df$csY = df$csY+1
df$rateX = df$rateX+1
df$rateY = df$rateY+1
length(unique(df$ppt))
```

# tag ppt that failed attention checks
```{r}
faile_checks <- c("553256591127375", "60916919062727", "115691198549233")
#not done T2
exclude_vals <- c("181158057290360")


df <- df %>%
  mutate(ppttype = case_when(
    ID %in% faile_checks ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ 1
  ))

passedcount <- df %>%
  group_by(ppttype) %>%
  summarise(count = n())
passedcount

df <- df[!(df$ID %in% exclude_vals), ]
length(unique(df$ID))
```



#useful functions & main vars
```{r}
GRID_SIZE <- 11

# Func to convert string dictionary to a valid JSON format
parse_func <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("'", "\"", x)
  parsed_list <- fromJSON(x)
  return(unlist(parsed_list))
}


parse_df <- function(json_str) {
  # Ignore `0` feedback
  if (is.na(json_str) || json_str %in% c("", "null", "0")) {  
    return(tibble(RUN = character(), saved = numeric()))  
  }
  
  parsed_list <- tryCatch(fromJSON(json_str), error = function(e) list())

  if (!length(parsed_list)) {
    return(tibble(RUN = character(), saved = numeric()))  
  }
  
  RUN <- names(parsed_list)
  saved <- as.numeric(unlist(parsed_list))

  valid_idx <- saved != 0
  RUN <- RUN[valid_idx]
  saved <- saved[valid_idx]

  # Ensure lengths match
  if (length(RUN) != length(saved)) {
    return(tibble(RUN = character(), saved = numeric()))  
  }
  
  tibble(RUN = RUN, saved = saved)
}

# Function to calculate Euclidean distance
euclidean_distance <- function(coord, pos) {
  if (length(coord) != 2 || length(pos) != 2) return(NA)
  sqrt((coord[1] - pos[1])^2 + (coord[2] - pos[2])^2)
}
```



Ratings 
# SPLIT HALF  

```{r}
#PRE RATINGS, T1
dfPRE <- df[df$state == "ratingPRE",]
D_pre <- dfPRE[dfPRE$Time == "T1",] %>%
  mutate(split = ifelse(run %in% c(0, 1, 2), "A", "B"))

# mean_ls for each split within each ID
D_split <- D_pre %>%
  group_by(ID, split) %>%
  summarise(mean_ratings = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = split, values_from = mean_ratings)

# split-half correlation across IDs
split_half_corr <- cor(D_split$A, D_split$B, use = "complete.obs")

# Spearman-Brown correction
spearman_brown <- 2 * split_half_corr / (1 + split_half_corr)

print(split_half_corr)
print(spearman_brown)

p <- ggplot(D_split, aes(x = A, y = B)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "T1/PRE: Correlation Between First and Second Half Ratings",
    subtitle = paste("Pearson r =", round(split_half_corr, 2), 
                     "| Spearman-Brown =", round(spearman_brown, 2)),
    x = "Mean Rating (First Half)",
    y = "Mean Rating (Second Half)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()+theme(aspect.ratio = 1)

print(p)

#T2
D_pre <- dfPRE[dfPRE$Time == "T2",] %>%
  mutate(split = ifelse(run %in% c(0, 1, 2), "A", "B"))

# mean_ls for each split within each ID
```

#Retest reliability 

https://cpsyjournal.org/articles/92/files/676294ae6f472.pdf
a) correlation between T1 & T2
b) ICCs
[c) of summary stats (ratings) & parameters (lambda)]


a) Summary stats: correlation between T1 & T2
```{r}
#ratings overall (includes PRE & POST)
faile_checks <- c("553256591127375", "60916919062727", "115691198549233")
dfICC <- df

#exclude ppt that did not pass questionnaire checks 
dfICC <- dfICC[!(dfICC$ppt %in% faile_checks), ]
length(unique(dfICC$ppt))

#get mean T1 & T2 ratings 
df_corr <- dfICC %>%
  group_by(ID, Time) %>%
  summarise(mean_ratings = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Time, values_from = mean_ratings)


# Correlate
t1t2_corr <- cor(df_corr$T1, df_corr$T2, use = "complete.obs")
res <- cor.test(df_corr$T1, df_corr$T2, use = "complete.obs", method = "pearson")
res

# Spearman-Brown correction
spearman_brown <- 2 * t1t2_corr / (1 + t1t2_corr)
print(t1t2_corr)
print(spearman_brown)

p <- ggplot(df_corr, aes(x = T1, y = T2)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#090049", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    subtitle = paste("Pearson r =", round(t1t2_corr, 2), 
                     "\nSpearman-Brown =", round(spearman_brown, 2)),
    x = "Outcome expectancy T1",
    y = "Outcome expectancy T2"
  ) +
  theme_classic()+
    theme(
    aspect.ratio = 1,
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14)
  )

print(p)

#ggsave(filename = "retest.png",path = file.path("..", "..", "plots"),width = 4,height = 4,dpi = 300,bg = "transparent")

```


```{r}
library(irr)
library(psych)

faile_checks <- c("553256591127375", "60916919062727", "115691198549233")
dfICC <- df
dfICC <- dfICC[!(dfICC$ppt %in% faile_checks), ]
length(unique(dfICC$ppt))


df_testconsistency <- dfICC %>%
  #group_by(ID, Time, csPosition, distance) %>%
  group_by(ID, Time) %>%
  summarise(mean_ratings = mean(rating, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Time, values_from = mean_ratings)
head(df_testconsistency)

# Run ICC(3,1) for test-retest reliability
#We used two-way ICCs, with a fixed effect of time, and a random effect of participant. These are equivalent to ICC(A,1) and
#ICC (C,1) (McGraw & Wong, 1996), and the consistency ICC is also known as an ICC(3,1) (Shrout &
#Fleiss, 1979)

#option 1 #0.54, 0.4 to 0.75 indicates moderate-good reliability
icc_result <- ICC(df_testconsistency[, c("T1", "T2")])
print(icc_result)

#option 2 #0.54
icc_pre <- icc(df_testconsistency[, c("T1", "T2")], model = "twoway", type = "consistency", unit = "single")
print(icc_pre)

```


#How about path length?
```{r}
average_moves <- dfICC[dfICC$state == "navigating",] %>%
  group_by(ID, Time) %>%
  summarise(nMoves = mean(nMoves, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Time, values_from = nMoves)


t1t2_corr <- cor(average_moves$T1, average_moves$T2, use = "complete.obs")
res <- cor.test(average_moves$T1, average_moves$T2, use = "complete.obs", method = "pearson")
res

icc_result <- ICC(average_moves[, c("T1", "T2")])
print(icc_result)

#option 2 #0.54
icc_pre <- icc(average_moves[, c("T1", "T2")], model = "twoway", type = "consistency", unit = "single")
print(icc_pre)



```


# Reliability of lambdas. 

```{r}
dflambdaT1 <- read.csv(paste0(data_path, "/data/retestT1/fitted_LSPRE.csv"),header = TRUE)
dflambdaT2 <- read.csv(paste0(data_path, "/data/retestT2/fittedT2_LSPRE.csv"),header = TRUE)

dflambda <- rbind(dflambdaT1, dflambdaT2)


#Split half and corr
dfsum <- dflambda %>%
  group_by(ID, time) %>%
  summarise(mean_ls = mean(mean_ls, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = mean_ls)
head(dfsum)

# split-half correlation across IDs
split_half_corr <- cor(dfsum$T1, dfsum$T2, use = "complete.obs")

# Spearman-Brown correction
spearman_brown <- 2 * split_half_corr / (1 + split_half_corr)

print(split_half_corr)
print(spearman_brown)

p <- ggplot(dfsum, aes(x = T1, y = T2)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, color = "#090049", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    subtitle = paste("Pearson r =", round(split_half_corr, 2), 
                     "\nSpearman-Brown =", round(spearman_brown, 2))
  ) +
  theme_classic()+
    theme(
    aspect.ratio = 2,
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 14),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA),
    legend.box.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA)
  )+xlab(expression("T1: fitted " * lambda))+ylab(expression("T2: fitted " * lambda))


print(p)
#ggsave(filename = "lsretest.png",path = file.path("..", "..", "plots"),width = 4,height = 4,dpi = 300,bg = "transparent")

#ICC

# Run ICC(3,1) for test-retest reliability
#We used two-way ICCs, with a fixed effect of time, and a random effect of participant. These are equivalent to ICC(A,1) and
#ICC (C,1) (McGraw & Wong, 1996), and the consistency ICC is also known as an ICC(3,1) (Shrout &
#Fleiss, 1979)

#option 1 #0.54, 0.4 to 0.75 indicates moderate-good reliability
icc_result <- ICC(dfsum[, c("T1", "T2")])
print(icc_result)

#option 2 #0.54
icc_pre <- icc(dfsum[, c("T1", "T2")], model = "twoway", type = "consistency", unit = "single")
print(icc_pre)
```
